stages.10: I have found a strange encampment built inside a crater east of Riverwood. It calls itself the Starfall Research Site. The guards told me to speak with Director Kast.
stages.20: Director Kast has sent me to Dr. Hale in the Test Chamber. Hale wants three Energy Crystals, which can be found in Embershard Mine near Riverwood.
stages.30: Dr. Hale was delighted with the crystals. Dr. Rusk, the site's nervous physician, asked me to recover his research journal from the sealed Containment Wing B, and gave me a keycard.
stages.40: I returned Rusk's journal. He revealed that Director Kast sealed Wing B during Incident Seven with six people still inside, then buried the report. I should confront Kast.
stages.50: Director Kast admitted to sealing Wing B. Whatever I make of his reasons, he granted me Directorate Clearance. Dr. Hale will now trade Energy Crystals with me, and the armory is open.

objectives.20: Bring 3 Energy Crystals to Dr. Hale
objectives.30: Recover Dr. Rusk's journal from Containment Wing B
objectives.40: Confront Director Kast about Incident Seven

journal.name: Rusk's Research Journal
journal.text:
Rusk, E. Personal research journal. Do not remove from Wing B.

12th of Last Seed, 4E 201
Specimen H-14 has stopped eating. It sits facing the north wall, toward the Test Chamber, and does not move. H-9 and H-11 are doing the same. I have told Kast. He wants it 'noted.'

15th of Last Seed
Hale is running the array at eighty percent tonight. Every parasite in the wing pressed itself against the glass ten seconds before the cycle began. Ten seconds BEFORE. They know. I don't know how, but they know.

17th of Last Seed
Asked Kast to postpone the full resonance test. He said the Directorate wants numbers, not nerves. Venn reinforced the bulkhead seals this afternoon. Nobody told him why. Nobody told me either.

19th of Last Seed
Incident Seven. I am writing this from my office with the door barred. The array hit peak at the eleventh hour. Every enclosure in the wing failed at once. The glass did not break. It simply was not there anymore.

Corvin was bitten near the hosts' pen. Dana dragged him clear. Two of Moran's officers came running from the east hall. Seven of us were still past the bulkhead when the alarms changed tone.

I reached the intercom. I told Kast we had seven people alive on our side. I told him we were coming.

He sealed the bulkhead anyway.

20th of Last Seed
I got out through the service duct. The others did not fit. I listened to them knock for most of the night.

22nd of Last Seed
Kast has filed the report. Wing B was 'unoccupied at time of seal.' He brought me the staff roster and asked me to sign it. I signed it. May whatever gods this land keeps forgive me, because I will not.

I am leaving this journal here, behind the seal, where it cannot be burned. If someone finds it, the truth is on these pages. I was not brave enough to say it aloud.

notes.title: Test Chamber Shift Log
notes.where: Test Chamber observation room, on the console desk
notes.text:
Shift log, Test Chamber, week of Sun's Height.

Day one: Array at sixty percent. Crystal three sang a clean tone for four minutes. Hale applauded. Venn did not.

Day two: Array at seventy. Minor rift flicker at the sample cradle. Something small and gray looked through. It looked back at us, then left. Hale wants to name it. Request denied.

Day three: Coolant line froze. Not from the cold. From the crystal. Venn says this is impossible. Venn has said that four times this week.

Day four: Pell fainted at the window. Ozone, probably. Possibly the gray thing again. Pell refuses to say.

Day five: Hale requested ninety percent. Director said no. Hale ran eighty-five 'by accident.' Logged as calibration error. It was not a calibration error.

Reminder to all staff: the observation glass is rated for pressure, not for headcrabs. Do not tap on it.

notes.title: Memo: Missing Prototype
notes.where: Director Kast's office, on his desk under a paperweight
notes.text:
INTERNAL MEMO. Director's office. Restricted.

To: Captain Moran, Dr. Hale

Following the Wing B event, a Zero-Point Field Manipulator prototype is unaccounted for. The armory log shows it signed out by a junior researcher who has since left the site without leave. Witnesses saw the individual heading west along the river road toward Riverwood, carrying a large bundle and, I am told, crying.

I do not want a search party. A squad of armored strangers kicking down doors in a Nord village will raise more questions than one missing device. The prototype cannot function without a charged crystal, and the locals will assume it is a strange farming tool.

If it surfaces, recover it quietly. If someone else is using it, observe them first. Anyone who can make that device work without training is worth knowing.

Dr. Hale: please stop referring to it as 'your baby' in official correspondence.

A. Kast, Site Director

notes.title: Requisition Form 14-C
notes.where: Venn's workbench in the generator room
notes.text:
REQUISITION FORM 14-C. Engineering.

Requested by: T. Venn, Chief Engineer

Items requested:
1. Copper wire, two hundred lengths. (Status: denied, rift unstable.)
2. Insulated gloves, six pairs. (Status: denied, see item 1.)
3. Any screw. Any screw at all. (Status: pending.)
4. A replacement for the hammer Hale borrowed and then threw through a rift. (Status: unrecoverable.)
5. Spare fuses, twelve. (Status: a local mage offered to 'be the fuse.' Declined.)

Justification: The resonance array is held together by optimism and a belt I bought in Whiterun. Generator two makes a noise I can only describe as grief. If this form is denied again, I will begin trading with the Riverwood smith directly, and I will not be sorry.

Approved by: ______

Note added by Director: Please use the form's actual fields, Tobias.

notes.title: Security Duty Roster
notes.where: Guard barracks, pinned to the wall by the bunks
notes.text:
DUTY ROSTER. Posted by Capt. D. Moran.

North fence: Officers two and five. Watch the ridge. Yes, the rock moves. No, you may not shoot it.

Gate: Officers one and seven. Do not accept mead, cheese, or marriage proposals from locals while on duty.

Canister bay: Officer four. Check every lid twice. If a lid checks you back, sound the alarm.

Test Chamber escort: Officer three. Stand behind Dr. Hale, not in front. You know why.

Wing B corridor: Nobody. Corridor is sealed. Do not knock on the door. Do not listen at the door.

Vent sweeps: Everyone, hourly. Complaints about vent sweeps go in the box marked 'Complaints.' The box is a brazier.

Reminder: the last person who called a headcrab 'cute' needed eleven stitches. Act accordingly.

Added underneath in a different hand: Who keeps taking the good helmet?

notes.title: Specimen Observations: Hollow Parasite
notes.where: Dr. Rusk's medical lab, beside the specimen tanks
notes.text:
Specimen observations, Dr. E. Rusk.

The parasite colloquially called a 'headcrab' is a jumping organism roughly the size of a bread loaf. It seeks the highest warm point of a target, which in most cases is the head.

Behaviour notes:
They are ambush hunters. They hide in vents, crates, and tall grass, and launch themselves at movement.
They avoid open flame but are not frightened by it. They simply wait for it to go out.
They prefer tall hosts. Nords are, I regret to report, ideal.
Once attached, the parasite binds to the host's nervous system within minutes. The host, which the guards call a zombie, continues to walk and attack, but responds to the parasite's hunger, not its own.

I have tested every tincture in the Riverwood alchemist's stock. None separate parasite from host. Removal kills both.

Most troubling: all specimens orient toward the Test Chamber when the array runs. I believe they hear it. I believe it calls them.

notes.title: Resonance Cascade Test Log
notes.where: Test Chamber control console, half burned
notes.text:
AUTOMATED LOG, RESONANCE ARRAY. 19th of Last Seed.

Ten past eleven: Cycle start. Target eighty percent. Operator: Hale.
Eleven sixteen: Eighty percent reached. Crystal tone stable.
Eleven seventeen: Operator override. Target raised to one hundred.
Eleven eighteen: Ninety percent. Harmonic drift in crystals two and five.
Eleven nineteen: Ninety-six percent. Sample cradle temperature falling. Frost forming on the cradle.
Eleven twenty: One hundred percent. Cascade detected. Rift aperture opening outside the chamber.
Eleven twenty: Secondary aperture detected in Containment Wing B.
Eleven twenty: Third aperture detected. Location unknown. Somewhere outside the crater.
Eleven twenty-one: Emergency shutdown requested. Shutdown failed.
Eleven twenty-two: Manual crystal ejection. Array offline.
Eleven twenty-three: Bulkhead B sealed by Director's override.

Operator comment, scrawled in ink beside the printout: It held. Gods help me, my chamber held. The others did not.

notes.title: Unsent Letter
notes.where: Inside sealed Containment Wing B, on a desk in the staff room
notes.text:
Dear Mira,

I am still not allowed to tell you where I am, so let's say it's cold, there are mountains, and the people here drink something called mead that would strip paint.

The work is good. Better than good. We found something here that could change everything back home. I wish you could see the crystals. They sing, Mira. Actually sing.

Things are tense this week. Dr. Rusk looks like he hasn't slept since spring, and the specimens keep staring at the walls. The Director says it's nothing. He always says it's nothing.

The alarms just changed. I'll finish this later.

I'll finish this later.

I love you. Tell Pip I'm bringing back a dragon tooth.

Dana

notes.title: Crumpled Courier's Note
notes.where: On a dead courier beside a cracked headcrab canister in the hills east of Riverwood
notes.text:
To whoever finds this,

I was carrying letters to Whiterun when I saw the metal thing fall out of the sky. Thought it was another piece of the falling star. Thought I'd be rich.

It was hot when I got to it. Hissing. The lid opened by itself. There was something inside, pale, with legs. It didn't move at first, so I poked it with my walking stick.

That was a mistake.

It went for my face. I knocked it off but it got my neck. The wound isn't bleeding right. It's going gray around the edges and my head feels too full.

The letters are in my satchel. Please deliver them. And if you see one of those things, don't poke it.

Tell my mother I didn't steal the cheese wheel from Lucan. Faendal did.

notes.title: Incident Seven: Evacuation Order
notes.where: Sealed Containment Wing B, posted beside the inner bulkhead
notes.text:
EMERGENCY ORDER. Containment Wing B.
Authority: Director A. Kast.

A containment failure is in progress. All staff are to proceed immediately to the east bulkhead.

The bulkhead will be sealed in five minutes.

Do not stop for equipment. Do not stop for specimens. Do not stop for colleagues who have been in contact with a host.

Once sealed, the bulkhead will not be reopened until the wing is confirmed clear.

This order supersedes all others.

Handwritten beneath, in a shaking hand:
It was not five minutes. It was two. We were at the door. We were AT THE DOOR.

And beneath that, fainter:
Six of us. Still knocking. Someone tell Rusk to tell them.

notes.title: The Lambda Directorate Wants You
notes.where: Site entrance lobby, in a stack on the reception desk
notes.text:
THE LAMBDA DIRECTORATE WANTS YOU!

Are you curious? Courageous? Comfortable with mild to moderate risk of being lifted off the ground?

Join the brightest minds of a distant world at Starfall Research Site, the premier crystal research facility in the entire province.

We offer:
Steady meals (soup).
Warm lodgings (warm-adjacent).
A front row seat to the future of energy.
Complimentary decontamination showers.
Generous hazard bonus, payable at end of contract.

We are seeking:
Laborers, haulers, and anyone who can lift a crate without asking what is inside.
Local guides familiar with the mountains east of Riverwood.
Mages, for comparison purposes only.

The Directorate is an equal opportunity employer. Nords, elves, and Khajiit welcome. Giants, sadly, cannot fit through the door.

Apply at the main gate. Do not approach the gate after dark. Officers may be nervous.

notes.title: The Falling Star: A Farmer's Account
notes.where: Riverwood, on a table in the Sleeping Giant Inn
notes.text:
As told by Gunnar Stone-Field, farmer, to anyone who'll buy him a drink.

I was mending my fence the night it came. The whole sky went white, brighter than Masser and Secunda put together. Then a sound like a thousand Thu'um at once, and the mountain to the east shook like a wet dog.

In the morning there was a hole in the world. Smoke for days. The goats wouldn't eat. The chickens laid eggs that glowed a little. My wife made me bury them.

Then the strangers came. Odd clothes, odd words, odd little lights that never go out. They built walls inside the hole and put men in masks to guard them.

They're polite, mostly. One of them, a quiet one, reads our sagas at the inn and asks good questions.

But I'll tell you this. Since they came, I've seen things in the hills. Pale things. Scuttling things. And once, a man walking with something on his head that wasn't a hat.

The Jarl says it's nothing. Jarls always say it's nothing.

notes.title: Hale's Manipulator Notes
notes.where: Dr. Hale's desk in the Test Chamber annex
notes.text:
Zero-Point Field Manipulator, design notes, rev. 9. M. Hale.

Principle: The crystal stores zero-point energy. The manipulator vents a controlled thread of that energy as a field. The field grips mass. The operator does the rest.

Pull mode: gentle, steady draw. Lifts crates, carts, and, in one memorable test, Venn's chair with Venn in it.

Punt mode: full discharge. Hurls the held object at speeds I am not yet allowed to measure indoors.

Power: one charged crystal per cell. Cells drain faster on heavy objects. Do not try to lift a mammoth. I have tried. The mammoth was not pleased.

Known issues:
The grip hums at a pitch that headcrabs seem to hate. Excellent.
The grip also hums at a pitch Kast seems to hate. Also excellent.

Prototype three is missing. If anyone finds it, please return it. She pulls slightly left. I love her anyway.

notes.title: Receipt of Sale
notes.where: Site archive, in a drawer of Venn's filing cabinet
notes.text:
Receipt of sale, witnessed at Windhelm.

Sold to: Wuunferth the Unliving, Court Wizard of Windhelm.
Sold by: T. Venn, on behalf of nobody, officially.

Items: Twelve pages of crystal resonance notes, copied by hand. Outdated, mostly harmless.

Payment: Three hundred septims, one bag of fire salts, and the wizard's word that he would not ask where we came from.

Venn's note on the back:
Needed the coin for parts. The Directorate will never pay for them. The old man studied the pages for an hour without blinking, then said something about 'trapping the song of the star.' A week later he was selling a spell that pulls energy from crystals. Not my problem. Probably. Do not tell Kast.
